title: People’s Mañanera August 31
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity’s Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available[here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Education Is a Right, Not a Privilege  
** More than 28 million students are returning to school with universal
scholarship/stipends covering elementary through high school. President
Claudia Sheinbaum was clear: “We don’t want anyone to drop out of school for
financial reasons. All children have talent.”

**Caring for Emotions Is Also a Form of Transformation  
** Through the ABCs of Emotions program, teenagers aged 14 to 18 will receive
mental health support, 16 million guidebooks, and one hour of instruction per
week in the classroom. The President declared that “together, we will support
them so they can continue to grow in a healthy way.”

**Mental Health Is Nurtured Within the Community  
** With 35,458 assemblies, health brigades, and care services at 100 Community
Centers, this support will reach every corner of the country. Faced with the
challenges posed by social media, Sheinbaum called for staying close to young
people, building trust, and supporting them without judgment.

**Less Screen Time, More Social Interaction  
** 81% of teachers agree that cell phones should not be allowed in the
classroom. Sheinbaum emphasized their effects on students’ attention span and
social interaction: “What we want is for them to play and socialize instead of
spending all their time scrolling,” the President explained.

**Decent Schools for Learning and Socializing  
** In Mexico City, the “1, 2, 3 for My School” initiative has a budget of 1.5
billion pesos (US$88.25 million) and has renovated 750 schools. The program
combines security, culture, technology, and scholarships/stipends to make
schools the best public spaces.
